items.concern: Transition from preoperational to concrete operational thought begins (concrete operations formally ~7–11, but the shift is gradual, not a light switch): early grasp of conservation; more logical though still concrete, not abstract, reasoning

items.concern: Transition into industry vs. inferiority (~6–11/12, Erikson): self-worth becomes increasingly tied to competence — schoolwork, sports, social skills — and to comparison with peers; repeated failure or excessive criticism at this stage risks a durable sense of inferiority; mastery experiences build the 'competence' virtue
items.guidance: Frame as the psychosocial task the parent is supporting, not a box to check — stage ages are canonical but soft (ESTABLISHED THEORY).

items.concern: Concrete operational stage (~7–11, Piaget): logical reasoning about concrete objects and events — mastery of conservation, reversibility, classification, seriation; reasoning still tied to tangible, real-world referents, and abstract/hypothetical reasoning is not yet reliable
items.guidance: Use as orientation for tone and complexity in copy, not a precise cutoff — stage transitions are gradual and individually variable (framework cross-cutting note).

items.concern: Industry vs. inferiority continues (Erikson): peer group and friendship take on much greater weight; sense of self increasingly includes social comparison ('am I good at this compared to others'); rule-based games with peers become important for learning fairness, negotiation, and resilience to losing
items.guidance: Frame as the psychosocial task the parent is supporting, not a box to check — stage ages are canonical but soft (ESTABLISHED THEORY).

items.concern: Sophisticated vocabulary growth via reading; understanding of multiple meanings; sarcasm and more abstract language use increase toward the end of the band
